hook: Your agent says it's done. How do you know it works?
pain: It passed its own tests. The ones it wrote, for itself.
idea: T S laws flips that. You write the rules, in plain TypeScript. The agent writes the code. And nothing lands until your rules hold.
write: A law is one line. Adding is the same either way around. Adding zero changes nothing. That's all you write.
run: Now run it. Three laws are proved, for every number there is. Not sampled. Proved.
catch: One fails. The agent's sort quietly drops duplicates. You get the smallest input that breaks it, and a seed to replay it.
lock: And the agent can't water your laws down. Change one, and the check fails. Only you can accept it.
browser: It works in a real browser too. Components, accessibility, speed. Live.
e2e: Even a whole app, server and all.
install: One install. Then every change your agent makes has to pass.
outro: T S laws. Trust the code you did not write.
